findings.text: High level decode entry derives instruction length from register context. It initializes a decoder over caller supplied bytes using current execution mode, replaces default size assumptions with code segment derived sizes, measures total length, and rejects empty decodes, attribute failures, or caller buffers shorter than measured length.

Code segment size query maps processor mode and current code selector to a packed size descriptor or a negative invalid argument signal. Virtual 8086 mode yields fixed narrow sizes, data segments and inconsistent long and default size combinations are rejected, remaining combinations yield distinct legacy and long mode width pairs.

Decoder initializer establishes bounded parsing context over caller memory. Overlong caller lengths are capped to architectural maximum, prior state is cleared, base and cursor and end markers are installed, operand width starts narrow, and address width starts wide in 64 bit mode and narrow otherwise.

Staged length and field decoders expose idempotent queries for prefixes, operation code grouping, register addressing, scaled indexing, displacement, immediate data, and total length. Each stage records completion to allow repeat calls, propagates shortage as missing data, and signals malformed grouping or addressing as invalid argument.

Packed size descriptor carries two widths in separate nibbles. Lower portion encodes operand width and upper portion encodes address width, with construction combining the pair and extraction isolating each portion.

Global descriptor lookup reads current table base and limit, derives table offset by ignoring privilege and table indicator bits of selector, rejects offsets beyond limit, and copies one table entry to caller on success with boolean status.

Local descriptor access is serialized by the address space context lock with narrow critical section around table pointer and entry count sampling and entry copy. Access is additionally gated by a non maskable interrupt safety predicate and by bounds validation against advertised entry count, returning failure without side effects when gated or out of range.

Non maskable interrupt access predicate reports safe only when per processor loaded address space matches current address space, with additional one time warnings for missing loaded state and for page table base mismatch against current control register value.

Prefix recognition progresses through emulation sequences, distinct legacy prefixes with size toggling effects, operand and address width extensions, and vector extensions with mode dependent exclusions. Legacy distinct count is bounded, last prefix identity is preserved with swap handling, and width overrides from extension bytes take precedence.

Addressing decode follows operation code to register addressing to scaled index to displacement to immediate progression. Register addressing presence refines group attributes, scaled index presence depends on address width and addressing mode and register field, displacement width depends on mode and address width and special register encodings, immediate handling covers memory offset, sized values, pointer and variable forms, and optional second byte.

Observed decoder state separates per field value, byte count, completion flag, and raw bytes, with an endian aware variant maintaining parallel numeric and little endian views. Cursor and bounds support lookahead and consumption, while attribute word and size widths evolve as prefixes and addressing are recognized.

Addressing byte layouts expose mode in high pair, register or opcode extension in middle trio, and register or memory selector in low trio, with scaled index base in low trio. Extension bytes expose width control in high bit for register extension and vector forms, and prefix selection in low pair for vector and extended operation forms.

Architectural instruction length ceiling is fifteen bytes. Code segment width pairs observed are two with two, four with four, and four with eight for operand with address respectively, with long and default size both set treated as invalid.

All forward reads validate remaining bounds before consumption and unwind to missing data on shortage, preventing overrun of caller buffer. Length query caches result and derives size from cursor displacement, while caller level decode additionally rejects buffers shorter than decoded length.

Group opcode refinement replaces generic attributes with register selected variant and clears attributes with invalid argument status when vector capable decoding encounters an extension that the refined attributes do not accept. Sixty four bit force attribute widens operand width late in register addressing stage.

Instruction attribute queries are pure bit tests over a table driven attribute word covering immediate presence and size class, second immediate, memory offset, register addressing requirement, group membership, sixty four bit force, variant availability, and vector extension acceptance.

Group attribute resolution selects a table by group identifier, indexes by middle register field of addressing byte, and when the base entry advertises prefix dependent variants and a last prefix identity exists, switches to the prefix specific table. Missing tables fall back to shared group bits, and last prefix identity derives from vector payload or legacy last byte through bounded mapping.
